Print the number of `sales` rows whose `customer_id` is no longer in the customer table, then the revenue of those rows (2 decimals), on one line as `rows revenue`. These rows would show as a blank customer in a visual.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
countries = ["UK", "Germany", "France", "Spain"]
cats = ["Hardware", "Software", "Services"]
customers = pd.DataFrame({
    "customer_id": range(1, 41),
    "customer_name": [f"Customer {i:02d}" for i in range(1, 41)],
    "country": [countries[i % 4] for i in range(40)],
    "segment": [["Retail", "Corporate"][(i // 4) % 2] for i in range(40)],

products = pd.DataFrame({

})
n = 400
sales = pd.DataFrame({
    "order_id": range(1, n + 1),
    "order_date": pd.to_datetime("2025-01-01") + pd.to_timedelta(rng.integers(0, 365, n), unit="D"),
    "customer_id": rng.integers(1, 41, n),
    "product_id": rng.integers(1, 13, n),
    "quantity": rng.integers(1, 6, n),

})
n = 400
sales = pd.DataFrame({
    "order_id": range(1, n + 1),

    "customer_id": rng.integers(1, 41, n),
    "product_id": rng.integers(1, 13, n),
    "quantity": rng.integers(1, 6, n),
})
sales["unit_price"] = (sales["product_id"].map(products.set_index("product_id")["unit_cost"]) * 1.5).round(2)
calendar = pd.DataFrame({"date": pd.date_range("2025-01-01", "2025-12-31")})

calendar["month_number"] = calendar["date"].dt.month

sales["revenue"] = sales["quantity"] * sales["unit_price"]
fact = (sales.merge(customers, on="customer_id").merge(products, on="product_id")

guided.title: Choose the dashboard visuals (written)
guided.prompt: For the sales dashboard, a stakeholder asks for: total revenue, revenue by month, revenue by category, revenue by customer for all 40 customers, and the share of the top five customers. Choose a visual for each, justify it with the rules of Day 133 and say which one would go on a drill-through page instead of the main page.
guided.starter:
Revenue: ...
By month: ...
By category: ...
By customer: ...
Top five share: ...
guided.solution: Total revenue is a single value, so a card. Revenue by month is a time trend, so a line chart (a column chart is acceptable for twelve points, but the line shows the slope). Revenue by category has three categories, so a column or bar chart sorted by revenue. Revenue by all 40 customers is too long for the main page: a horizontal bar chart limited to the top ten with a table or drill-through page for the rest, so the main page stays uncluttered. The top-five share is one number, so a card, with a short label such as 'Top 5 customers' share of revenue'. The customer-level detail is the item to move to a drill-through page, because it is for investigation and not for the first read.
rubric: Sorted bar or column for categories and top-N bar for customers.
hints: How many customers fit on a page?
What is for the first read and what for investigation?

]

def overlaps(a, b):
    return (a["x"] < b["x"] + b["w"] and b["x"] < a["x"] + a["w"]
            and a["y"] < b["y"] + b["h"] and b["y"] < a["y"] + a["h"])

def problems(page):
    out = []
    for v in page:
        if v["x"] + v["w"] > 1280 or v["y"] + v["h"] > 720:
            out.append(v["name"] + ": off canvas")
        if any(v[k] % 40 for k in ("x", "y", "w", "h")):
            out.append(v["name"] + ": not on grid")
    out += [f"{a['name']} overlaps {b['name']}" for i, a in enumerate(page) for b in page[i + 1:] if overlaps(a, b)]
    return out

print(len(page))
print(problems(page))

independent.title: Handover note (written, stretch)
independent.prompt: Write the handover note for the sales dashboard for the analyst who will maintain it: the data model and checks, the measures with their expected values, the visuals and their purpose, the security design and the open publishing items. It should fit on one page.
independent.starter:
Model: ...
Measures: ...
Visuals: ...
Security: ...
Open items: ...
independent.solution: Model: star schema with `Sales` (400 orders in 2025) related to `Customers` (40), `Products` (12) and a continuous `Calendar`; checks: unique order ids, all keys resolve, calendar has 365 days. Measures: Total Revenue 67,132.50; Orders 400; Units 1,202; Average Order Value 167.83; Price per Unit 55.85; Revenue YTD at December equals the total; Top 5 Customer Share 0.2148, each tested against pandas. Visuals: three cards (revenue, orders, average order value) for the headline, a monthly line chart for the trend, a category bar for the mix, and a top-customers table, laid out on a 40 pixel grid with the revenue card top left. Security: a dynamic role on Customers that uses a hidden UserSecurity table; the four country views add up to the total. Open items: assign role members in the Service, schedule and test the refresh, publish the app and name an owner for refresh failures.
rubric: Describes the model and its validation checks.
Explains each visual's purpose and the layout rules used.
States the RLS design and the reconciliation.
Lists open publishing items with an owner.

environment.note: The dashboard itself is built in Power BI Desktop (Windows-only) and published to the Power BI Service (browser); neither runs in this course. This project produces the verified specification and numbers to build from, and the graded exercises check the model, the measures and the layout rules with pandas and Python.

checks.question: A customer id in Sales is missing from the Customers table. What happens in a visual by customer name?
options: Power BI stops with an error
The revenue shows against a blank customer, and the total is still right
The row is deleted from Sales
checks.explanation: Power BI keeps the fact row and assigns it to a blank member of the dimension. Totals are unchanged, so the problem is easy to miss without a key check.

checks.question: Why compute each measure's expected value in pandas?
options: To have an independent check of the measure's filter logic
Because pandas is part of Power BI
checks.explanation: An independent calculation catches wrong filters or relationships; copying the measure's own result into a test would prove nothing.

checks.question: The four country views of a RLS role add up to 66,000 while the total is 67,132.50. What does that mean?
options: Some rows are not covered by any role filter, for example a country missing or a customer without a country
checks.explanation: Restricted views should partition the data. A gap means rows that nobody sees, such as customers with blank or unexpected values in the filter column.

checks.question: Which layout problem does check_layout report when the trend ends at x = 800 and the bar starts at x = 760?
checks.explanation: The two rectangles share the x range 760 to 800 and the same y range, so they overlap. Moving the bar to x = 800 or less width fixes it.

checks.question: Which item of the final checklist can only be done in the Service?
checks.explanation: Role members and refresh schedules are set in the Service. The other items can be verified before publishing.
